clips.title: Build & deploy agents with the Claude Agent SDK
clips.why: Why context windows fill up, and how specialised subagents keep the main agent's context small.
look: What fills a context window during a long agent run.
Why a helper that reads many files and returns a short summary helps the main agent.
clips.after: Nova's reader helpers do exactly this: they read widely and hand back a few file:line pointers.

clips.title: Most devs don’t understand how context windows work
clips.why: Matt explains the lost-in-the-middle problem: a model pays less attention to what sits in the middle of a long context.
look: Where in a long context the model attends best, and where worst.
Why a shorter, focused context can give a better answer than a longer one.
clips.after: A judge with only the ticket and the diff has nothing in the middle to lose, which is one more reason to keep its inputs small.

clips.title: LLM as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation Strategies
clips.why: The main ways to use a model as a judge, and how to choose between them.
look: The difference between judging one answer against a rubric and comparing two answers.
How the choice of strategy depends on what you want to decide.
clips.after: Our scope judge is the rubric kind: one diff, a fixed list of what to veto, and a verdict in a schema.

clips.title: LLM as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation Strategies
clips.why: The weak spots of model judges: the biases to watch for before you trust a verdict.
look: Which biases are named, and which of them could hurt a judge that reviews code.
clips.after: A fresh context removes the worst bias, the author's own memory; checking judges against people's labels handles the rest.

practice.q: Convert the zod schema so the SDK accepts it.
practice.hint: The JSON Schema version the SDK validates with.
practice.why: Without the target, zod declares draft 2020-12, and the SDK refuses schemas newer than draft-07.

practice.q: What does a subagent receive when Nova delegates to it?

options.why: A normal subagent starts fresh. It does not see the parent's history or tool results.

options.text: Its own system prompt and the prompt string Nova writes for it
options.why: That string is the only channel from parent to helper, so put every path or decision the helper needs into it.

options.text: Nothing but the files in the working folder
options.why: It also gets its own system prompt and the delegation prompt, and can read files with its tools.

practice.q: Put the steps of the judge function in order.
items: Build the prompt from the ticket and the diff only
Start a session with no tools, no settings and a plain system prompt
Pass outputFormat with the draft-07 schema
Wait for a success result that carries structured_output
Parse it with the zod schema and return the typed verdict, or throw
practice.why: The inputs are fixed by our code first; the verdict is accepted only when it exists and parses.

practice.q: The judge's result has subtype error_max_structured_output_retries. What happened?

options.text: The model kept producing JSON that did not match the schema
options.why: The SDK re-prompted on each mismatch and gave up after its retries. Simplify the schema or the task.
An invalid schema fails the run at startup with an error naming the problem.

options.text: The judge used too many tool calls
options.why: A judge with tools: [] makes no tool calls. This subtype is only about the output format.

practice.q: Stop helpers from starting helpers of their own.
practice.hint: One layer of helpers below the main agent.
practice.why: 1 allows one layer of subagents and no nesting. The default is 3 layers.
